chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān from al-Ḥalabī said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the night prayer and the witr prayer at the beginning of the night while traveling, if I feared the cold or if there was an ailment. He said, 'There is no harm; I do it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine night and witr prayers when traveling and fearing cold or illness?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith illustrates the principle of *rukhas* (divine concessions) within Shia jurisprudence, where physical hardship justifies modifying the timing of voluntary night prayers. Imam al-Sadiq’s personal affirmation ('I do it') serves as a strong evidentiary precedent (*shahada*) for the permissibility of performing Witr and Salat al-Layl at the start of the night rather than delaying them until dawn when cold or illness is a concern.
